title: if you haven’t gone back to the kit kat club now is the time! #cabare...
transcript: I have seen five different casts in this production of cabaret I don't think I have ever loved a cast as much as this one eva noblezada and orville peck who play Sally Bowles and the emcee make a lot of bold choices that are vastly different from the people that came before them I am a tad bit biased because I love Eva so much as a performer but when I tell you all of her strengths when it comes to her singing her acting, her humour are like perfectly tailored for Sally Bowles Eva has this incredible like duality of being able to put on a show so like when you see her interact with cliff or Schulz or Schneider Peak Sally bowles like big over the top ultimate manic Pixie dream girl but then anytime that she's on stage by herself you watch her like crack open you see this Sally Bowles that is vulnerable that is insecure and that is deeply deeply afraid and I ate it up her maybe this time I was weeping she wants cliff to be this thing that she is missing and she's like maybe the thing that I'm missing inside me I can find in this person oh it destroyed me and then you get to cabaret and is the opposite and watch her like dig back in and put on that mask and go back out into the world and it is oh this gutting and the vocals never heard cabaret sung with that kind of intensity and fierce spark and she like yowls Elsie oh it it destroys me I truly do not know anything about Orville Peck before they cast him in this role and now I am a super fan I'm obsessed with the way that he plays the emcee obviously he's a performer so I was not worried about like the performance aspect of the emcee vocals are great you cannot take your eyes off of him when he is on the stage but it was the acting that like he just really nailed in a way that I was not prepared for his emcee is scary like he really plays in to the emcee as the villain Adam Lambert who was also obsessed with made almost like the opposite choice I felt like his emcee was trying to warn people but in the only way he could which was to like play along and hope that people could see it and something about making the choice to play the emcee as a bad guy really just worked for me especially with Eva playing Sally so much more vulnerable he doesn't wear the mask from minute one which made me a little bit a little bit sad because I was like I kinda like the idea of him wearing the mask and then taking the mask off but he is a beautiful man I've been a little bit mixed on this production of cabaret but the more times I see it the more I think it hits there are things about this production of cabaret in terms of the way that Rebecca Fracknell sees all of us as complicit that really hit me differently because of everything that is happening in America right now so many people don't want to pay attention and they for lack of a better word want to go to the cabaret and they wanna just pretend that's not happening and go on with normal life when really like we have to fight back and we have to talk about it we have to be loud the line I keep coming back to is “don't you see if you're not against it you're for it” anyway go see cabaret
showTitle: Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club
classificationReason: Creator explicitly states 'I have seen five different casts in this production of cabaret' and shares detailed first-hand opinions about Eva Noblezada and Orville Peck's performances, specific emotional reactions, and acting choices.
